quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What should you know about eye protection?

options.text: It is not needed if your motorcycle has a windshield.
It is only needed in bad weather.
It must allow you to see clearly to both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: It must allow you to see clearly to both sides.
questions.explanation: California law requires proper eye and face protection. A face shield protects your face if you crash. Good eye or face protection must let you see clearly to both sides.

questions.question: What should you do if you ride on a slippery surface?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, reduce your speed. Avoid sudden moves. Use both brakes gently.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Change lanes to let them pass or slow down to create more space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to let them pass or slow down to create more space.
questions.explanation: Ride in a way that lets the tailgater pass you. Speeding up only makes them tailgate you faster, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: What should you check when choosing a helmet?

options.text: It has no cracks or defects.

questions.correctAnswerText: It has no cracks or defects.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snugly and be free of cracks, loose padding, and frayed straps.

questions.question: What is true about a DOT-approved helmet?

options.text: It allows you to see far enough to the sides for safe riding.
It can be a danger to the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: It allows you to see far enough to the sides for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet does not limit your vision. It allows you to see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: What helps prevent crashes?
questions.correctAnswerText: Using proper lane positions.
questions.explanation: To prevent crashes, be visible, signal your turns, keep safe distance, look ahead at least 12 seconds, spot hazards, and stay ready to react.

questions.question: What gear should your motorcycle be in when you start it?
questions.correctAnswerText: Neutral.
questions.explanation: Always put your motorcycle in neutral before starting the engine. Most motorcycles have a light on the speedometer that shows when you are in neutral.

questions.question: What should you know about blind spots on motorcycles?

options.text: They don't exist if you have a rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should check them regularly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?
questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden movements if possible.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, sudden speed or direction changes can cause a skid. Accelerate, shift, turn, and brake as smoothly as possible.

questions.question: How should you handle a tailgater?

options.text: Let them pass by slowing down or changing lanes.
Speed up to create distance between you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let them pass by slowing down or changing lanes.
questions.explanation: If you can do so safely, change lanes or slow down to let the tailgater pass. Speeding up only makes them tailgate you faster, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.
Only stop to let other traffic pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely. Let all traffic and pedestrians pass. Then go when it is safe.

questions.question: Your motorcycle should fit you. This means:

options.text: Your fingertips barely touch the handlebars when you sit on the bike.
The seat is one foot higher than your waist when you stand next to the bike.
Your feet touch the ground comfortably when you sit on the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your feet touch the ground comfortably when you sit on the bike.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle fits you correctly if your feet touch the ground comfortably while you sit on it. Make sure your bike fits you before you ride.

questions.question: The best way to avoid tiredness on a long motorcycle ride is to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Take frequent breaks to rest.
questions.explanation: To avoid getting tired on a long ride, limit your riding time each day. Take frequent rest breaks. Do not use artificial stimulants because you may feel very tired when they wear off.

questions.question: To help other drivers see you, you should:

options.text: Use your headlight only at night or in poor conditions.
Use your headlight at all times.
Add an orange tint to your headlight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your headlight at all times.
questions.explanation: Using your headlight at all times is the best way to help other drivers see your motorcycle.

questions.question: To reduce the chance of a crash, you should:

options.text: Focus only on your riding, not your surroundings.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright or reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Wearing bright or reflective clothing helps other drivers see you and reduces your risk of a crash. Always stay aware of other drivers around you.

questions.question: When riding, you should wear:
questions.correctAnswerText: Bright clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing to be more visible when riding, even during the day. Reflective clothing also helps.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, your position in the lane:

options.text: Does not affect whether other drivers can see you.
Is very important because it affects whether other drivers can see you.
Cannot protect you from wind from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is very important because it affects whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Your position in the lane helps other drivers see you. It also helps you avoid wind blasts from other vehicles.

questions.question: Do not ride directly next to another vehicle because:

options.text: The driver may want to use your lane to pass.
You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
You may have an escape route.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because you may be in the driver's blind spot. The driver will not see you. Also, the vehicle may block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: If vehicles are on both sides of your motorcycle, which lane position is best?
questions.correctAnswerText: Center
questions.explanation: No lane position is always best. A good rider changes position based on road and traffic conditions. If vehicles are on both sides, the center position is usually safest.

questions.question: When riding during the day, you should:

options.text: Wear dark clothes because it is light outside.
Wear bright clothes so other drivers see you better.
Be comfortable, wearing shorts if it is hot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothes so other drivers see you better.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Wear bright clothing when riding during the day to help other drivers see you.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both the front and rear brakes at the same time with controlled pressure.

questions.question: What should you wear when riding a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Full-fingered gloves.
questions.explanation: Wear full-fingered gloves made of durable material. They give you a better grip and protect your hands.

questions.question: Is it safe to ride directly beside another vehicle?

options.text: Yes, because you are in a separate lane.
Yes, because it blocks the wind.
No, because you may be in the driver's blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, because you may be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Do not ride beside other vehicles. You may be in their blind spot, and the driver might move into your lane without seeing you.

questions.question: If you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlight to signal the other vehicle to go.
Continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: What is true about motorcycle footrests?

options.text: The driver and passenger can share them.
They are required for the driver and passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are required for the driver and passenger.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles must have footrests for both the driver and passenger. Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance and safety.

questions.question: When scanning the area around your motorcycle, what should you look for?

options.text: Potential escape routes near intersections, shopping areas, or schools.
Whether you can travel faster than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Potential escape routes near intersections, shopping areas, or schools.
questions.explanation: Look for escape routes in and around intersections, shopping areas, schools, and construction zones.

questions.question: What danger does wind noise create?

options.text: It is easy to get used to.
It can permanently damage your hearing.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can permanently damage your hearing.
questions.explanation: Long-term exposure to wind noise can permanently damage your hearing. Use ear plugs or hearing protection when riding.

questions.question: How is alcohol different from other beverages?
questions.correctAnswerText: It enters the bloodstream immediately.
questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested. It goes directly through the stomach and small intestine into the bloodstream and quickly reaches the brain.

questions.question: When entering a turn, when should you change gears?

options.text: Take the motorcycle out of gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before entering the turn. If you must change gears while turning, do it smoothly.

questions.question: What should you do when nearing a blind intersection?

options.text: Assume that other drivers will properly yield the right-of-way.
Change your lane position to be more visible to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position to be more visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: Move into the lane position that makes you most visible to other drivers at a blind intersection.
